pos.personaBrief: Flamengo 2022 liked to dominate the ball (A Gazeta, Driblab) and Santos 2010 attacked openly, so possession and control are favored over ceding the ball.

pro.personaBrief: Elaborate attacking football inherited from Jorge Jesus (Driblab) with lots of movement and passing triangles; not reliant on long balls, though simple and objective.

est.personaBrief: Systems looked rigid but had constant movement and position swaps (Drible de Corpo 2022); Santos 2010 had freedom of movement, so relational leaning.

lar.personaBrief: Flamengo used Marinho as a right winger and Cebolinha open on the left; Santos had Robinho and Neymar on the flanks, but also a diamond with Arrascaeta centrally.

blo.personaBrief: Flamengo pressed the opponent's build-up and recovered quickly in the opposition half (Driblab, A Gazeta), a high-block team.

mar.personaBrief: No source states the marking scheme; the collective reduction of space in recomposition suggests zonal, space-based defending.

pla.personaBrief: He did not reinvent things, kept a simple own model with the same attacking dominance regardless of opponent, adjusting through rotation; the team plays its own way.

res.personaBrief: Offensive, ball-dominant teams that press for the goal; but results-focused in a hot-seat context, aiming to win rather than draw.

sis.personaBrief: He accommodated Ganso, Neymar, Robinho and Gabigol in roles, with stars working tactically (Everton Ribeiro recomposing), simple system, and benching Neymar.

jog.personaBrief: Technical teams (Ganso, Arrascaeta, Neymar), with a place for the creator, though intensity and collective commitment were part of Flamengo's play.

bas.personaBrief: He boosted academy youngsters like Victor Hugo and Neymar-era talent under pressure, while using a rotated squad full of veterans and signings at Flamengo.

lid.personaBrief: Good player relations (players thanked him), accommodating stars but the Neymar clash in 2010 shows he enforced rules, even costing his job.
